A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FATE and provide readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be reliably matched across the added appendix sections and renumbered displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on 20 subjects, component ablations, neural-baking trade-offs, and qualitative completion, editing, and reenactment results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds camera-noise robustness results, computational measurements, and expanded ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed sampling-based densification, personalized blendshapes, BakeNet, losses, and SphereHead completion procedure remain unchanged. The revised pipeline clarifies where optional completion fits; the alternative densification procedures are experimental controls.

E1.justification: The same 20 subjects from INSTA, PointAvatar, NerFace, and EmoTalk3D are retained. Section 11 adds a distinct test scenario with inaccurate camera translations; there is no new dataset or application task.

E2.justification: The principal comparators remain FlashAvatar, SplattingAvatar, MonoGaussianAvatar, and GaussianAvatars. New Table 7 adds GA-based and SA-based densification alternatives within the component comparison; Figure 15 additionally compares FATE with GaussianAvatars under camera noise.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Gaussian camera-translation perturbations at sigma values of 0.5, 1, 2, 5, and 10 mm as labelled in Figure 15, plus training-time/FPS evaluation under identical hardware conditions and additional ablation controls. Existing benchmark preprocessing and stated training/testing budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and baking trade-off study, Sections 11–13 add pose-noise robustness and computational analysis, pruning-only and alternative-densification controls, and expanded yufeng/bala ablations with Gaussian counts. Appearance-only baking already existed in v1; its new quantitative coverage extends that analysis.

E5.justification: The existing plus/minus Gaussian-count summaries are retained and reused in Table 6. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. The noise sigma values specify experimental perturbations.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–4 and the per-subject tables remain unchanged; v1 Tables 5–6 become v2 Tables 8–9. Substantial new results cover robustness, timings/FPS, and expanded ablations in Figure 15 and Tables 5–7; for example, Table 6 reports FATE at 1.0 hour training and 203 FPS on INSTA. Figures 1 and 9 also substitute logo-editing examples.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and derivations are retained. Equation 7 relabels indices without changing the normalized sampling formula; no new assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical properties are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same three contributions, state-of-the-art performance claim, and claimed first animatable 360-degree full-head reconstruction from monocular video. The shortened conclusion preserves their substance.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies consistent, uniform lighting as an applicability limitation and attributes observed noise robustness to UV embedding constraints. It also interprets the new efficiency and densification comparisons. Identity changes, intricate-geometry failures, and baking/editing trade-offs were already discussed in v1's appendix.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future code release with a project/code access link. Section 12 newly reports one completion epoch, five baking epochs, and component runtimes; these are disclosures rather than established changes to previous settings. Existing detailed hyperparameters remain available in the appendix.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references, including Mani-GS, DialogueNeRF, and IDOL, and adjusts their placement in the literature discussion. It trims the PanoHead/SphereHead discussion, including the characterization of SphereHead as the most suitable prior, while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits include localized wording corrections, clarification of the pipeline, a condensed conclusion, acknowledgements, and an updated appendix overview incorporating three new sections. The main narrative and existing appendix organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 2 now depicts optional completion, Figures 1 and 9 update editing examples, and Figure 15 and Tables 5–7 are added. Table 6 redisplays Gaussian counts alongside timing/FPS columns. Existing appendix displays are retained and renumbered, with limited resizing and repositioning.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the efficiency and densification arguments with direct computational measurements and additional controls, while adding robustness evidence and clearer limitations. These are useful, targeted gains. An unresolved reporting discrepancy limits confidence in one added result: Table 7 gives appearance-only baking on bala a PSNR of 29.53, whereas retained Table 4 gives 28.76 with matching SSIM and LPIPS and no explained setting difference.
